  • 9b) Analyse how the relative importance of internal and external influences varies across different
  • purchase situations. Discuss the influence of personal factors, psychological factors, family
  • reference groups, culture, social class and marketing stimuli on high-involvement and low
  • involvement purchase decisions, with suitable examples.
  • Introduction and Explaining Internal and external factors and Involvement (8 marks)
  • • Consumer buying behaviour is influenced by a combination of internal and external factors.
  • Internal influences arise from the individual consumer, while external influences originate from
  • the consumer's social, cultural and marketing environment.
  • • Internal influences include personal factors such as age, income, occupation, lifestyle and
  • personality, and psychological factors such as motivation, perception, learning, attitudes and
  • beliefs.
  • • External influences include family, reference groups, culture, social class and marketing stimuli
  • such as product features, price, advertising and promotional offers.
  • The relative importance of these influences varies according to the level of consumer involvement, the
  • nature of the product, the perceived risk and the purchase situation.
  • High-involvement purchases: decisions in which consumers invest considerable time and effort because
  • the product is expensive, personally important, unfamiliar or associated with significant risk. Consumers
  • usually engage in extensive information search and careful evaluation. Example: Purchasing a car
  • selecting a college, buying a house or choosing a health insurance policy.
  • Low-involvement purchases are routine decisions involving relatively little perceived risk, financial
  • commitment or personal importance. Consumers generally make these purchases quickly, often relying
  • on habits, familiarity and convenience. Example: Purchasing toothpaste, biscuits, soap, salt or a familiar
  • brand of packaged food.
  • The importance of internal and external factors differs between these two types of purchases.
  • Comparative Analysis of Internal and External Influences
  • Influencing
  • Factor
  • High-Involvement Purchase Decisions Low-Involvement Purchase Decisions
questions.final_answer: High-Involvement Purchase Decisions Low-Involvement Purchase Decisions

questions.question: b) Explain the relationship between customer satisfaction and customer loyalty. Why may a satisfied customer still change brands?
questions.solution_html:
• Proposal solicitation: Inviting quotations, proposals or tenders.
  • Or any other relevant explanation
  • LONG ESSAY QUESTION
  • Answer one question from the pair (a / b). The question carries 20 marks.
  • 9a) What are the stages of the Family Life Cycle? Explain the importance of family and
  • households in consumer buying behaviour.
  • Suggested pointers for the answer: (marks as indicated against each part)
  • Introduction (2 Marks) : Meaning of family and household and the difference between them; family
  • life cycle (FLC) as a classification of households by age, marital status and presence/age of children.
  • FLC stages (13 marks)
  • • Bachelor stage: young, single, living apart from parents; spend on fashion, entertainment
  • gadgets, travel.
  • • Newly married couples (honeymooners / DINKs): high purchasing power; spend on furniture
  • vacations, durables, insurance.
  • • Full nest I: youngest child under six; home purchase, baby products, health and education
  • savings.
  • • Full nest II: youngest child six or older; family packs, education, sports, entertainment.
  • • Full nest III: older couples with dependent children; replacement of durables, higher
  • education spending.
  • • Empty nest I: children have left, head still working; travel, hobbies, luxuries, home
  • improvement.
  • • Empty nest II / retired: reduced income; health care, medical products, leisure.
  • • Solitary survivor: single older person; health care, companionship, security. Modern variants
  • (single parents, childless couples, live-in households) may also be credited.
  • Importance of Family and Households in Consumer Buying Behaviour (5 marks)
  • Joint Purchase Decisions: Many household purchases involve discussions and decisions
  • among family members. For example, purchasing a car, refrigerator or house may require
  • agreement between spouses.
  • Culture Cultural values and traditions can
  • strongly influence important purchases
  • associated with marriage, education
  • housing and family responsibilities.
  • Example: Indian wedding traditions
  • influence the purchase of gold jewellery.
  • Culture shapes everyday consumption
  • habits and familiar product preferences
  • often without conscious evaluation.
  • Example: Consumers regularly purchase
  • rice, spices and traditional food products
  • according to cultural habits.

  • 8b) A young professional purchases an expensive branded handbag because she believes it will
  • improve her social image and make her feel more confident. Identify the relevant buying motives
  • and explain how they influence her purchase decision.
  • Suggested pointers for the answer: (identification of motives 3 marks for three relevant motives with
  • explanation; explanation of influence on decision 2 marks) Mark liberally.
  • The young professional's purchase of an expensive branded handbag is primarily influenced by
  • emotional buying motives (such as prestige, status, self-esteem and self-confidence) and rational
  • motives (Quality, durability, brand reputation)
  • Emotional Motives
  • • Social image / prestige motive: Desire for status and approval from others; linked to esteem and
  • social needs (Maslow); conspicuous consumption.
  • • Confidence / self-esteem motive: Need to feel confident and enhance self-concept; the brand
  • acts as a symbol of identity.
  • • Social Acceptance Motive: The desire to create a favourable impression and gain recognition
  • from others may also influence her decision.
  • Rational / product-related motives
  • • Quality, durability, brand reputation and assurance (if mentioned).
  • How Buying Motives Influence Her Purchase Decision: Motives create the need, make social and
  • emotional attributes more important than price, and narrow evaluation to prestige brands.
  • Influence on Product Usage: Household size and composition determine the quantity and
  • types of products purchased. For example, a large family may prefer bulk grocery packs and
  • larger household appliances.

questions.question: Apex Motors, a high -end automobile manufacturer, recently introduced the "Terra GT," an electric SUV. Apex historically catered to rugged, outdoor -oriented drivers. However, for the Terra GT, marketing framed the vehicle as "Sophisticated Luxury for the El ite Professional." Apex priced it at $85,000, placed advertisements in high -end business journals, and selected minimalist, gallery-style showrooms with highly formal sales staff. Page 3 Simultaneously, Lumina Tech released a smart home assistant called "Echo Sphere." During its pre-launch, Lumina ran high-energy TV spots featuring energetic music and humorous scenarios to drive engagement. However, in the first month post-launch, customers suffered frequent server outages and app crashes. While early buyers found the advertisements fun, overall reviews plummeted due to reliability failures. A perceptual mapping analysis comparing Terra GT, Echo Sphere, and key competitors revealed the following positioning insights: • Terra GT: Consumers perceived it as overpriced and excessively formal, leaving a gap in its traditional "rugged, highly durable utility" space. Existing Apex owners expressed confusion over who the brand was trying to be. • Echo Sphere: Consumers rated the product high on "Excitement" due to its advertising, but exceptionally low on "Competence" due to functional failures. Questions a. Explain the elements of the consumer perception process in the context of Apex's Terra GT. How did Apex's marketing mix cues (use 4 Ps of marketing) lead to perceptual distortion among traditional Apex customers? b. Based on the case, analyse how Apex can use perceptual mapping for Market Segmentation and Brand Repositioning to address customer confusion. c. Using Aaker’s Brand Personality framework, contrast Lumina Tech's marketing image with its real product performance. What identity conflict did this create for consumers?
